QBI: Compulsory IFR Flight Rules - A term indicating that Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) are mandatory for flight operations, typically due to weather conditions or airspace requirements.
RAPID: Rapid or Rapidly - A descriptor used in aviation weather reports and forecasts to indicate that changes in weather conditions are occurring or expected to occur quickly.
RASH: Rain Showers - Precipitation consisting of rain that starts and ends suddenly, often with rapid changes in intensity, associated with convective cloud activity.
RASN: Rain and Snow - A mixed precipitation type consisting of both rain and snow falling simultaneously, which can create hazardous icing conditions for aircraft.
SNSH: Snow Showers - Precipitation consisting of snow that starts and ends suddenly, often associated with convective clouds and gusty winds.
TAANS: Transmits or Transmitter - A device or action related to transmitting radio signals in aviation communications and navigation systems.
TRLVL: Transition Level - The altitude above mean sea level at which aircraft change from using local altimeter pressure setting (QNH) to the standard pressure setting (1013.2 hPa) during climb.
TSGR: Thunderstorm with Hail - A thunderstorm accompanied by hail (ice pellets), which poses significant hazards to aircraft including structural damage, icing, and severe turbulence.
YD: Yard - A unit of distance measurement used in certain aviation contexts, particularly in runway length and visibility reporting in some regions.
SH: Shower - A prefix used in ICAO weather codes to indicate precipitation of an intermittent nature with rapid onset and cessation, followed by the precipitation type (e.g., SHRA = rain showers).
...M: Metres - The standard unit of length measurement in aviation, used for reporting runway visual range (RVR), visibility, altitude, and other distance measurements, preceded by numerical figures.
A/A: Air-to-Air - A designation for communications or operations between two or more aircraft, such as air-to-air radio frequencies or air-to-air refueling.
A/G: Air-to-Ground - A designation for communications or operations between aircraft and ground stations, including air-to-ground radio transmissions and data links.
AAD: Assigned Altitude Deviation - The deviation of an aircraft from its assigned altitude, typically monitored by air traffic control for separation assurance.
AAL: Above Aerodrome Level - A height measurement referenced to the elevation of the aerodrome, used for obstacle clearance and traffic pattern altitudes.
AAR: Air-to-Air Refueling - The in-flight transfer of fuel from one aircraft (tanker) to another (receiver), extending the range and endurance of the receiving aircraft.
ABI: Advance Boundary Information - A notification sent to air traffic control units providing advance information about an aircraft that is approaching their area of responsibility.
ABM: Abeam - A term indicating that an aircraft or object is positioned at a right angle to the longitudinal axis of another aircraft, typically used in position reporting.
ABN: Aerodrome Beacon - A rotating or flashing light located at an aerodrome to help pilots visually identify the airport location during night operations or low visibility conditions.
ABT: About - A term used in aviation communications to indicate an approximate value, time, or location.
ABV: Above - A term used in altitude reporting and weather phenomena descriptions to indicate a position higher than a specified reference point.
ACFT: Aircraft - Any machine that can derive support in the atmosphere from the reactions of the air, including airplanes, helicopters, gliders, and balloons.
ACK: Acknowledge - A request for confirmation that a message has been received and understood, used in aviation radio communications.
ACL: Altimeter Check Location - A designated point on an aerodrome where pilots can verify the accuracy of their altimeter setting against a known elevation.
ACN: Aircraft Classification Number - A number expressing the relative effect of an aircraft on a pavement (runway, taxiway, or apron) for pavement strength evaluation.
ACPT: Accept or Accepted - A term used in air traffic control communications to indicate agreement to a clearance, instruction, or request.
ADA: Advisory Area - A designated airspace area within which advisory services are provided to participating aircraft regarding traffic and navigation.
ADC: Aerodrome Chart - A detailed plan view of an aerodrome showing runways, taxiways, aprons, buildings, and other facilities, used for ground navigation.
ADDN: Addition or Additional - A term used in NOTAM and aviation communications to indicate supplementary information or an extra item.
ADF: Automatic Direction Finder - A radio navigation instrument that automatically displays the bearing to a selected non-directional beacon (NDB) station.
ADJ: Adjacent - A term used in aviation to describe a location or area next to or nearby a specified point, airspace, or facility.
ADR: Advisory Route - A designated route along which advisory service is provided to aircraft to assist with traffic avoidance and navigation.
ADVS: Advisory Service - A service provided by air traffic control to aircraft operating in advisory airspace, offering traffic and navigation information on an advisory basis.
ADZ: Advise - A term used in aviation communications requesting or providing a recommendation or notification regarding operational matters.
AES: Aircraft Earth Station - A satellite communication terminal installed on an aircraft that enables communication with ground stations via satellite for voice and data services.
AFIL: Filed in the Air - A flight plan that is submitted by a pilot via radio communication after the aircraft has already departed.
AFS: Aeronautical Fixed Service - A telecommunications service between specified fixed points for the safety and regularity of air navigation, including AFTN and other ground-based networks.
AGL: Above Ground Level - A height measurement referenced to the underlying terrain or surface, used for obstacle clearance, traffic patterns, and instrument approach minima.
AGN: Again - A term used in aviation communications to request repetition of a message or to indicate a repeated action.
AIC: Aeronautical Information Circular - A notice containing information on aeronautical matters that does not qualify for NOTAM publication but is important for flight safety.
AIREP: Air Report - An in-flight weather report transmitted by an aircraft crew to provide meteorological observations and conditions encountered during flight.
AIS: Aeronautical Information Services - A service responsible for the collection, processing, and dissemination of aeronautical information necessary for flight safety and navigation.
ALA: Alighting Area - A designated area on water or land used by aircraft for landing and takeoff operations, such as a seaplane base.
ALRS: Alerting Service - A service provided by air traffic control to notify appropriate organizations about aircraft in emergency situations and to coordinate search and rescue efforts.
ALS: Approach Lighting System - A system of lights installed on the approach end of a runway to provide visual guidance to pilots during the final approach phase.
ALT: Altitude - The vertical distance of an aircraft above mean sea level (MSL), measured by an altimeter and used for vertical separation and terrain clearance.
AMA: Area Minimum Altitude - The minimum altitude that provides adequate terrain and obstacle clearance within a specified area for instrument flight.
AMS: Aeronautical Mobile Service - A radio communication service between aircraft stations and ground stations, or between aircraft stations, for aviation safety and regularity.
AMSL: Above Mean Sea Level - A reference altitude measured from the average level of the sea surface, used as a standard datum for aircraft altimeters and terrain elevation.
ANS: Answer - A response to a call or query in aviation communications, confirming receipt of information or providing the requested data.
